topStories.headline: DA Charges Man With 10 Hot-Prowl Burglaries Targeting Pacific Heights and Presidio Heights Homes
topStories.dek: A 38-year-old San Francisco man was arraigned Tuesday on residential burglary and related charges after prosecutors say he broke into occupied homes across Pacific Heights and Presidio Heights over a month-long spree.
topStories.body:
San Francisco District Attorney Brooke Jenkins announced on October 28 that Levi Michael Banks, 38, has been charged with ten counts of residential burglary, along with vandalism, possession of stolen property, and theft of access cards and card information. Prosecutors say the alleged crimes — known as hot-prowl burglaries because they are committed while residents are inside and asleep — took place between September 26 and October 23, 2026, striking homes in Pacific Heights, Presidio Heights, and Noe Valley.

Two Pacific Heights homes bore the heaviest losses. Prosecutors allege that Banks stole more than $64,000 in property from residences on the 2500 block of Fillmore Street and the 2200 block of Jackson Street on October 13. Investigators said they identified a suspect vehicle through automated license plate reader data after Banks allegedly made fraudulent purchases with victims' stolen credit cards.

The arrest came in the early hours of October 23, when officers responded to a triggered silent alarm on the 3700 block of Clay Street near the Presidio border. Police surveilled the suspect's vehicle and took Banks into custody when he returned to it around 4:36 a.m. A backpack found nearby contained roughly $4,500 in cash, victims' personal identification, and clothing that matched surveillance footage from the burglary scenes.

Banks was arraigned Tuesday and is scheduled to appear in court again on November 3. The district attorney's office said the investigation remains active and that additional charges are possible. All charges are allegations; Banks has not been convicted. Anyone with information is asked to call SFPD at 415-575-4444 or text Tip411 with the message beginning 'SFPD.'

topStories.headline: District 2 Is on the Ballot Tuesday — Sherrill Faces No Serious Challenge, But the Safeway Fight Looms
topStories.dek: Incumbent Supervisor Stephen Sherrill heads into the November 3 general election for District 2 — which covers the Marina, Cow Hollow, Pacific Heights, and Presidio Heights — having already won his seat convincingly in June.
topStories.body:
Tuesday's citywide general election includes the District 2 seat on the San Francisco Board of Supervisors, the district that represents the Marina, Cow Hollow, Pacific Heights, and Presidio Heights. Incumbent Stephen Sherrill, who was appointed by then-Mayor London Breed in December 2024 and then won a June special election with roughly 70 percent of the vote, is running again to serve a full term.

Sherrill, a former director of the Mayor's Office of Innovation, has positioned himself as a moderate voice on housing, public safety, and small-business support. He was an early and vocal opponent of the proposed 20-story residential tower at the Marina Safeway site, though critics in his June race argued he had not done enough to block the project. The Safeway lawsuit — filed in September by a coalition of neighborhood groups — is still working its way through federal court and is likely to remain a backdrop to local politics through next year.

Polls open at 7 a.m. Tuesday. Registered voters can also drop off mail ballots at any San Francisco Elections Department drop box through 8 p.m. on Election Day.

topStories.headline: Chestnut Street Is About to Get an All-Day Café From the Team Behind Norcina and Frankie's
topStories.dek: Kait Bauman and Angelo De Lorenzi plan to open Scout, an upscale all-day California café, in the former L'mida space at 2359 Chestnut Street in early November.
topStories.body:
The duo behind Norcina restaurant and Frankie's cocktail bar are expanding their Marina footprint with Scout, a daytime café planned to open on Chestnut Street in early November. Bauman and De Lorenzi will take over the former L'mida space at 2359 Chestnut St., rounding out what has become a growing collection of Marina spots from the same team.

Scout is described as an all-day California café, extending the team's reach into morning and afternoon service after Norcina anchors the Italian dinner hour and Frankie's handles the late-night cocktail crowd. The opening adds another option to a Chestnut Street corridor that has seen steady restaurant turnover — including the May closure of longtime Italian stalwart Ristobar after 22 years — and a string of newer arrivals.

Construction on the Scout space was nearing completion as of mid-October, according to Hoodline's reporting. No exact opening date has been publicly confirmed beyond 'early November.'

moreNews.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory Covers Marina Waterfront Through Saturday
moreNews.body: A National Weather Service Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 29 covers San Francisco Bay shoreline areas — including the Marina Green and Crissy Field waterfront — through 6 p.m. Saturday, November 1. High tide at the San Francisco gauge was expected around 1:43 p.m. Thursday, running roughly 1.9 feet above normal, with up to 1.9 feet of inundation possible near tidal waterways. Residents and visitors walking or cycling the Bay Trail along the Marina should expect wet or impassable sections at peak tide times through the weekend.
